{
  "title": "The Book That Returns",
  "world": "cinematic storybook realism — tactile, believable, gentle wonder",
  "cold_open": "Every ten years, a book returns to the library, always by a reader who never seems to age.",
  "question": "Who is this reader, and why does the book return, always on the same day, untouched by time?",
  "journey": "A young librarian notices the book's return, its pages unchanged, and the same name written in the catalog. Curiosity drives him to follow the pattern through decades of records, each entry marked by the same name, the same date, and the same quiet return. He tracks down the book's history, finding that it was never checked out, yet always returned — as if it had been waiting.",
  "discovery": "He finds a photograph in the library's archives — a child, no older than ten, holding the book. The child's face is familiar, but he can't place it. He searches further and finds a journal hidden inside the book's cover, filled with entries from the same child, written in a careful, steady hand.",
  "emotional_turn": "The librarian realizes with a start that the child in the photograph is himself, decades younger — and the book was always meant to return to him. He feels the weight of the moment, as if time itself had been watching, waiting for him to remember.",
  "payoff": "The book returns once more, and this time, he is the one who returns it — unchanged, just as the reader before him. He steps outside, the snow falling softly, as if the world had been holding its breath for this moment.",
  "after_image": "The librarian walks through the empty library, the book in his hands.",
  "hero_shot": "The librarian stands at the library's threshold, the book clutched tightly, as the first snowflakes fall silently around him."
}
